line: Hi there. Ray Treviño, Treviño Insurance, on Grand next to the bakery. And you are?
Welcome to the neighbourhood. Good handshake, by the way. You'd be surprised how many people don't have one.
choice1: What brings you to the hall?

line: The softball team. I pay for the uniforms, so {homeLead} lets me come and say hello. Sunday we lost twelve to two, but we looked great.
choice2: What kind of insurance do you do?

line: Auto, home, renters, a little life. Mostly auto. If you rent, get renters. It's twelve bucks a month and nobody ever regrets it.
choice1: How long have you done it?

line: Thirty years. My dad had a body shop on Fifth, so I knew cars before I knew English. Well, almost before.
Monterrey, till I was nine. First week of school the teacher read the roll and said 'Raymond.' I said yes. Been Ray ever since.
For what? Raymond was easier for the teacher, for the bank, for everybody. Including me.
Thirty years I've sold policies on the phone. People hear 'Ray' and they relax. They hear an accent and they ask for my supervisor. I don't have a supervisor.
Fair, not fair. It's how it is. You can complain about it, or you can be very, very good on the phone. I picked the phone.
Tyler and Megan? No. Tyler's at State, accounting. Megan wants to be a dentist. My kids won't need any of this, and that's fine.
choice2: Do they come to the hall?

line: The hall, the Spanish, the dance. It's good, I'm not knocking it, I still pay for the uniforms. But what they need is a good credit score and a firm handshake. They've got both.
You can't miss what you never had. $ [neutral] Listen, I've got a client at ten. Come by the office sometime, I'll give you a pen.
Hi, are you here for the benefits session? Ray Treviño. Your HR hired me to explain the dental plan.
Short version? Take the one with the cleanings. Two cleanings a year, nobody ever regrets the cleanings.
choice2: The one with the cleanings. Got it.
choice3: Thanks. I have to get back.

line: No commission on this one, I promise. HR pays me a flat fee. I do it because half the people here sign the first page and never read the second.
The deductible, the waiting period, the part where your kid's braces aren't covered. In English, in eight-point type. Read the second page, {playerName}.
choice1: Do people ask you about it in Spanish?

line: Some do. I answer in English, slowly. They understand fine. People learn faster when they have to. That's how I learned.
Maybe. But the second page doesn't come in Spanish, and it isn't going to. Better they can read it. Questions, I'm by the cabinet.
Hey, {playerName}. Back for more dental?
Forty people, three questions. 'Is it free,' 'Is it free for my wife,' and 'Where's the coffee.' I answer the third one best.
choice1: And the answer to the first?

line: Nothing's free. The cleanings are close. Real advice? Take the full retirement match. That's the only free money in this building.
Morning. Coffee? The hall's urn makes it like motor oil. I respect it.
Morning. Coffee? The hall's urn makes it like motor oil. I respect it.
{homeLead}. Officially the parish, really {homeLead}. She'd run the Chamber too if they let her, and they should.
Sure. She walks people over to the library, the clinic, city hall. Right direction. $ I just tell her, skip a step, take them straight to the bank. She says I'm a man in a tie. I am a man in a tie.
{homeLead}. If you ask anybody over sixty, and that's most of the hall.

Good man, I mean it. Fixed the boiler for free, twice. But he runs it like this room is the whole world. $ [guarded] My kids came to one Club dinner. He asked Tyler why he doesn't speak Spanish. Tyler didn't know what to say. I did. I didn't say it.
Lost twelve to two on Sunday. The uniforms looked great. I paid for the uniforms. My job is done.
choice2: Twelve to two is a lot.

line: Guys from the parish, a couple of dads, the Mendoza grandson. Don Aurelio comes to every game and yells at the umpire in Spanish.
Sure. We disagree about everything except softball. He thinks I gave up too much. I think he's keeping a room his grandkids won't need. We sit together at the games anyway.
For him? No. The Club is good for Don Aurelio. For the grandson I want the bank, the Chamber, a good résumé. He can come back for the dance.
{playerName}. Got a minute? Free advice, from a guy who learned it the hard way.
You're putting a résumé together, right? Everybody is. Let me see it sometime.
First thing, the hall goes under 'Community,' not 'Cultural.' Same work, same Saturdays. It reads different to a hiring manager.
Because 'Community' says you show up. 'Cultural' makes them guess what you are. Don't make them guess. $ [guarded] I'm not saying it's right. I'm saying it works.
Chamber board, eleven years. Office on Grand with my name on the window. Tyler's at State. _a pause_ Yeah. It worked.
Chamber of Commerce breakfast, Thursday, seven a.m. You free?
Bankers, a dentist, Frank from the hardware store, eggs that sat out a while. I want to bring someone young who gets it. That's you.
Hey. Long week. My phone hasn't stopped.
choice3: I'll let you take your calls.

line: Half my clients are calling to ask if their auto policy asks about status. It doesn't. I've said 'it doesn't' maybe sixty times.
Some. I tell them what I tell everybody. Pay on time, drive the limit, registration in the glove box. Be boring. Boring is safe.
_quiet for a moment_ No. Not always. But it's what I can sell them, and it's mostly true. The rest, I send them to {homeLead}.
Did you see? The state is putting the insurance forms out in Spanish now.
Fine. Good for some people. I'll keep sending mine in English.
People learn faster when they have to. I did. Nobody gave me a form in Spanish in 1984.
choice1: Or they sign things they can't read.

line: Okay. If they ask, I'll read it to them. In English, slowly. That's my compromise and I'm sticking to it.
Every time I come to the hall, you're here.
Good people. Good coffee, if you like motor oil. But don't spend every Saturday in one building.
The city's bigger than Grand. The people who hire you, lend you money, rent you an office, they're on Fifth. Go meet them. The hall will still be here.
Frank DeLuca says he sees you around Fifth.
Hardware store. Chamber treasurer, knows everybody's business. If Frank knows your name, you're doing fine.
That's how it works. Five years from now nobody asks where you started. They ask what you do.
_smiles_ They ask about the name. Treviño, with the squiggle. I tell them it's a family business. That's true, and it's all they need.
Ray checks his phone.
Water under the bridge. I've had worse from clients. Handshake?
Hey, {playerName}. Good to see you. How's the car? Do you have a car?
Then you're saving money. Renters insurance, though. Twelve bucks a month. I say it to everybody, so I'm saying it to you.
choice1: How long have you been selling insurance?

line: Can't stop, I've got a client at ten about a hail claim. Hail! In October.
